translation.text: Examine all the works in heaven, how they do not change their ways, and the lights in heaven: how they all rise and set, all ordered, each in its season, and do not transgress their order.[a]

footnotes.text: This follows the selected Charles 1906 Ethiopic print on printed page 6 (PDF44), including its two source stars and parenthetical conjunction. The selected rising form is ይሠርቁ. Actual Dillmann 1865 columns 239-240 support rising and 963-964 setting; 243-244 support ordering, 1041 season/time, 1011-1012 transgression, and 715-716 the two negatives. Charles note 1 reports an emended opening and equates it with Greek κατανοήσατε; note 3 says the lost conjunction was supplied on Greek authority. Only those bounded edited inputs are adopted and recorded separately, not the facing Greek festival clause or an alternative ordering construction. The English preserves both negatives and the repeated all/each relation. This is a low-confidence edited-print treatment, not independent manuscript certification.

translation.text: Look in summer and winter, how all the earth is filled with water, and cloud, dew and rain rest upon it.[a]

footnotes.text: This renders the selected Charles 1906 Ethiopic on printed page 6 (PDF44), preserving its one source star before all the earth. The final selected verb is transcribed የዐርፍ after direct 600 dpi inspection, including the prefix የ; its prefix must not be reconstructed from the English sense. Actual Dillmann 1865 columns970-971 support the resting sense, while columns131,834,149,217,212,1091,1214 and1053-1054 support summer, winter/rainy season, filled, earth, water, cloud, dew and rain. Summer and winter are the selected terms, not a modern climate correction. All the earth, the final feminine upon-it relation, and all three cloud/dew/rain terms remain. This is an edited-print translation, not independent manuscript certification.
